newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes says flights may not resume Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes says flights may not resume Thursday.

text.p: Great Lakes Aviation Ltd said Tuesday that it may not be able to resume flying by Thursday, as the grounded airline had earlier hoped.

U.S. Federal Aviation Administration officials had inspected several of the regional carrier's 53 airplanes as of Tuesday and talks continued on a consent order that would set forth required changes, said airline and FAA officials.

Asked if Great Lakes still hoped to resume limited flights by Thursday, airline senior vice president for marketing Dick Fontaine said, "It probably is going to be a little later than that, but I won't know until we get a determination."

Spencer, Iowa-based Great Lakes voluntarily suspended all flights Friday after the FAA informed the carrier that it faced a suspension of its operating authority due to flying "unairworthy aircraft." Great Lakes operates commuter flights for UAL Corp's United Airlines and for Midway Airlines.

Great Lakes said Tuesday that six FAA inspectors were at its Spencer base and, along with company employees, were "working diligently and cooperatively through a thorough review and inspection process."

Fontaine said, "We've got a number of aircraft inspections completed. We're winding up a couple, but I don't know what the status of them is." He added that he expected to be briefed on the inspections later in the day.

The FAA said it was working on a consent order that would detail what Great Lakes must do to comply with FAA regulations. "I don't think we could expect it before the end of the week," said FAA spokeswoman Rebecca Trexler.
